title: Child Development Progress Review & Reassessment | PinnacleAI
lead: The next step should make sense to your family. See what your child can do now, understand the support that helps, and leave the review knowing what you and the team will work on next.
directAnswer: Reassess, Review and Repeat is Pinnacle’s cycle for comparing the child’s present abilities with the earlier picture, interpreting everyday observations with the family, and agreeing what to continue, adapt or reconsider. AbilityScore® and the seven Readiness views contribute to that discussion. The professional explains the next goal, suitable support and when to review it again.
lifePurpose: A self-sufficient, mainstream-included life is the purpose from the beginning. Your child’s communication, daily routines, learning and participation give every measurement, therapy goal and review its direction.

illustrativeExample.title: Packing a bag is one task. Joining the school day is the purpose.
illustrativeExample.intro: Illustrative example: a five-year-old and their family are working toward taking part in the school-morning routine. The example below explains a decision. It is not a patient record or a prescribed programme.

observations.label: The earlier picture
observations.title: An adult does the packing.
observations.setting: At home, before leaving for school.
observations.support: The parent gathers the items and puts them in the bag.
observations.response: The child watches and joins when invited.
observations.meaning: The record needs to show the help provided, as well as what the child does.

observations.label: What the family notices now
observations.title: A picture sequence helps at home.
observations.setting: A familiar table, with the items within reach.
observations.support: The same short picture sequence; the parent points to the next item.
observations.response: The child follows the cue and places the item in the bag.
observations.meaning: Useful participation with picture and adult support. Independent packing has not been established.

observations.label: The different setting
observations.title: School arrival still needs a different approach.
observations.setting: A busy arrival area; teacher input shared with permission.
observations.support: The parent takes over the bag while the child waits nearby.
observations.response: The home routine has not been observed in this setting.
observations.meaning: The family and professional need to understand the setting before expecting the same response.

illustrativeExample.comparison: A prompted step at a quiet home table and a busy school arrival are different observations. The review keeps the activity, setting, support and child’s response together. It asks what became easier in life and what still needs a useful change.
illustrativeExample.decision: In this example, the occupational therapist discusses the routine with the family and, with permission, the school. They keep the useful home picture sequence and agree to try one bag step in a quieter arrival spot, with one familiar adult and the same picture cue. The child can pause or ask for help. The goal is comfortable participation in the arrival routine.
illustrativeExample.family: The parent uses the agreed picture sequence during an ordinary morning opportunity, offers the support discussed with the therapist and notices what the child chooses to attempt. The family brings back what was useful, what was difficult and any sign that the task or setting needs to change.
illustrativeExample.checkpoint: At the next agreed review, compare the steps attempted and completed, the picture or adult help used, the setting and the child’s comfort. The quieter-arrival adjustment has not yet been tried in this example; its result is open. Agree the review date with the responsible professional.

branches.title: Continue what is useful
branches.text: If the child participates comfortably with the agreed support, the team can retain it and discuss another relevant opportunity. Any change in help is planned with the professional.

branches.title: Adapt the support or setting
branches.text: If a step remains difficult, review access to the bag, the cue, timing, adult help and the environment. Choose a specific adjustment and say what the next observation should answer.

branches.title: Reconsider the goal or assessment
branches.text: If comfort, participation or abilities change, the professional and family can pause the activity, revisit the goal, assess further or arrange an appropriate referral. More repetition is a decision to justify.

illustrativeExample.status: Fictional explanation; not a patient result, prescribed plan or completed follow-up. The proposed support response remains unobserved.

reviewCycle.title: Reassess the starting picture
reviewCycle.text: Compare the relevant abilities and readiness information with the earlier record. Describe the measure, setting and help provided.

reviewCycle.title: Review what life tells us
reviewCycle.text: Bring family observations together with professional interpretation and relevant, consented school input.

reviewCycle.title: Explain the next decision
reviewCycle.text: Agree the goal, support to continue or change, family practice and the reason for the choice.

reviewCycle.title: Return to the next checkpoint
reviewCycle.text: Look for the agreed response, discuss what happened and revise the plan toward greater participation.

stages.title: Understand capabilities
stages.text: Identify what your child can do now and what support is involved.

stages.title: Plan toward readiness
stages.text: Discuss a meaningful goal and a child-specific, revisable plan.

stages.title: Connect relevant therapies
stages.text: Bring the needed professional contributions around that goal.

stages.title: Practise in daily life
stages.text: Use suitable everyday opportunities with family guidance.

stages.title: Track and correct
stages.text: Bring observations back into professional review.

stages.title: Reassess and repeat
stages.text: Compare change and explain what should happen next.

stages.title: Keep life as the direction
stages.text: Work toward self-sufficiency and mainstream participation.

familyPreparation: One everyday activity you want your child to take part in more comfortably.
What your child attempted or did, where it happened and who was there.
The picture, cue, equipment or adult help that was provided.
Your child’s choices, comfort, preferences and wish to pause.
Questions about the next goal, home practice and review date.

therapyContributions.name: Speech Therapy
therapyContributions.text: Review how a request, choice or way to ask for help works with different people.

therapyContributions.name: Occupational Therapy
therapyContributions.text: Review activity access, movement, sensory and environmental support for daily routines.

therapyContributions.name: ABA & behavioural support
therapyContributions.text: Review the context around behaviour, communication, comfort and the response to support.

therapyContributions.name: Special Education
therapyContributions.text: Review learning access, teaching supports and participation in classroom routines.

questions.question: What is a child development progress review at Pinnacle?
questions.answer: It is a discussion of the child’s present abilities, relevant measurements and everyday observations, compared with the earlier picture. The family and responsible professional agree what to continue, adapt or reconsider, what to practise and when to review the next response.

questions.question: How does reassessment connect with a self-sufficient, mainstream-included life?
questions.answer: Growing independence and participation give the plan its direction. A review asks whether a capability is becoming useful in communication, daily routines, learning or life with others, and what support is appropriate next. Each child’s goals, pace and outcomes differ.

questions.question: How often should my child be reassessed?
questions.answer: Agree the schedule with the responsible professional. Pinnacle’s documented methods describe monthly reassessment in one programme; the appropriate timing for an individual child depends on the measure, goals, circumstances and agreed care plan.

questions.question: What should our family bring to a progress review?
questions.answer: Bring one specific everyday example, the activity and setting, what your child attempted or did, the help provided, and your child’s comfort and choices. Bring relevant existing reports and questions about the next goal, practice and review date. Use the agreed private care channel.

questions.question: What if AbilityScore or a Readiness view does not improve?
questions.answer: A score is one part of the discussion. Check whether the same measure and conditions are being compared, what support was offered and what changed in everyday life. The professional can review the goal, support, assessment needs and next checkpoint with the family.

questions.question: Can a skill look different at home and school?
questions.answer: Yes. People, noise, timing, activity and adult support can differ. Describe those conditions rather than assuming the skill has transferred. Relevant school observations can inform review when shared with appropriate permission.

questions.question: Does the plan change automatically?
questions.answer: No. Measurements and observations inform professional interpretation. The responsible professional discusses appropriate changes with the family and explains the next observation or reassessment.

questions.question: Can we reduce, pause or change an activity?
questions.answer: Bring the child’s comfort, choice and response into review. The professional and family can discuss retaining a useful support, adapting or pausing an activity, changing a goal or arranging further assessment. The appropriate decision depends on the child.

questions.question: Do the regulatory licences guarantee independence or school admission?
questions.answer: No. MD-5 defines the software’s non-diagnostic intended use and the BIS record defines its documented scope. A score change or licence does not guarantee independence, school admission or a particular outcome. Actual participation and the child’s support needs guide review.

questions.question: How can we arrange a conversation with Pinnacle?
questions.answer: Call 9100 181 181, choose a Pinnacle centre or use the enrolment page. Tell the team one everyday priority and ask about a suitable professional, first visit, fees and review process. Your enquiry starts a conversation; the team confirms the visit arrangements.
